messages:
Amber: FYI we're seeing repeated p99 spikes on a subset of requests during microbursts. Not typical load — looks like short bursts trigger kernel fallbacks and then KV cache misses.
Ravi: Can you paste a sample trace? Which kernel fallback are you seeing? :thinking: 
Amber: snippet from traces: 
```
fallback: aten->fallback_cuda_kernel
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.42
queue_delay_ms: max=26 p95=18 p99=45
max_wait_ms config=10
```
Jun: That queue_delay p99 of 45ms during bursts makes sense if max_wait_ms is low; microbatching doesn't fill before timeout so kernels get cold and fallback to slower path.
Maya: Agreed. Also noticed KV eviction around the same time — backend logs show inflight key churn. Might be race between prefix prefetch and fallback path clearing cache.
Ravi: Two levers to try quickly: increase `max_batch_tokens` to let batches form during bursts, and bump `max_wait_ms` to reduce premature flush. Proposed quick test: 
```
scheduler:
  max_batch_tokens: 8192  # was 4096
  max_wait_ms: 25        # was 10
  microbatch_target: 256
```
Theo: +1 to experimenting but let's run an A/B so we can measure p95/p99 and throughput. We should watch tail-latency (p99.9) and per-model kernel fallback count.
Amber: I'll run a 30m A/B on the canary fleet. Metric targets: p95 < 30ms, p99 < 70ms, throughput delta < -2% (we can tolerate a small drop).
Jun: Quick profiling notes: when kernel fallback happens we see a ~1.8x token-processing slowdown and 30–60ms extra latency due to kernel handshake + cache warm. Suggest instrumenting fallback counter and KV cache hit timeline.
Maya: Question: do we need to tune quantized kernel selection thresholds as well? Some fallback triggers are model-length dependent.
Ravi: Good point — add a sampling job that records sequence-length vs kernel route. Also add `kv_prefetch=true` for canary to see if improving cache warm helps.
Amber: infra-bot started canary deployment job #bld-2026-314
infra-bot: Deployment bld-2026-314 to canary cluster started by Amber. Monitoring enabled: scheduler metrics, kernel_fallback_count, kv_cache_hit_rate.
Theo: After 30m, collect these: p50/p95/p99, kernel_fallback_count, kv_cache_hit_rate, tokens/s, and compare to baseline. If p99 improved and fallback fell >50% we promote to more nodes.
Jun: If we still see tail spikes after config tweak, next steps: 1) add small adaptive backoff that raises `max_wait_ms` during detected microbursts, 2) add fast-path kernel warming (keep-alive small queries to warm kernels), 3) KV write consolidation to reduce churn.
Amber: Running the canary now. Will post results (short summary + graphs) in ~40m. :thumbsup:
